title: A Bernstein-type inequality for translates of powers of a cosine bump
statement:
Let $(\lambda_n)_{n=-\infty}^{\infty}$ be a strictly increasing sequence of real numbers. Define

$$
H(x)=
\begin{cases}
\cos x,& |x|\le \pi/2,\\
0,& |x|\ge \pi/2.
\end{cases}
$$

For a positive integer $M$, suppose that the sequence satisfies the **gap condition**

$$
\lambda_{n+M}-\lambda_n\ge \pi
$$

for all $n$. For every finite sequence $(a_n)$ of real numbers, set

$$
G(x)=\sum a_n H^M(x+\lambda_n).
$$

**Bernstein-type conjecture.** The function $G$ satisfies

$$
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|G'(x)|^2\,dx\le M^2\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}|G(x)|^2\,dx.
$$

This conjecture generalizes the preceding inequality for a single power $H^M$, which follows from Bernstein's inequality for trigonometric polynomials via the substitution $T(x)=\sin^M x$. The claim asks whether the same $L^2$ derivative bound remains valid for arbitrary finite linear combinations of translates whose locations obey the stated gap condition; the supplied text gives no resolution.
source_name: Vilmos Komornik and Paola Loreti, “A Bernstein type inequality”, arXiv:1003.1278 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1003.1278

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2010).

title: Monotonicity of potential means along Dirichlet eigenfunctions
statement:
For the Dirichlet eigenfunctions $u_j$ of $-\Delta+V$ on a bounded convex domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ with convex potential $V$, normalize the eigenfunctions in $L^2$ and define

$$\langle V\rangle_j=\int_{\Omega}V u_j^2\,dx.$$

Are the means $\langle V\rangle_j$ an increasing sequence as $j$ increases? The report notes that the question is already interesting in one dimension.
source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2009/06, page 70
references: Source: [10.4171/OWR/2009/06](https://ems.press/journals/owr/articles/3389), page 70. Canonicalized from 1 source-backed detection(s); richer provenance is retained in the corpus artifact.

title: Convexity and reciprocal concavity of the coupon-collection objective function
statement:
Let $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and, for positive $x_1,\ldots,x_N$, define

$$
p_N(x_1,\ldots,x_N)=\int_0^1\left(1-\prod_{i=1}^N(1-t^{x_i})\right)\frac{dt}{t}.
$$

**Convexity and reciprocal-concavity conjecture.** For each $N\in\mathbb{N}$, the function $p_N$ is convex; indeed, $1/p_N$ is concave. This claim concerns the network objective function arising in coupon collection and predicts a generalization of the verified low-dimensional partial-fraction patterns.
source_name: Francisco J. Aragón Artacho, Jonathan M. Borwein, Victoria Martín-Márquez and Liangjin Yao, “Applications of Convex Analysis within Mathematics”, arXiv:1302.1978 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.1978

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2013).

title: Cummings–Feng boundary Korn inequality for elastic Helmholtz solutions
statement:
Let $\Omega$ be the domain with boundary $\Gamma$, and let $\mathbf{H}^2(\Omega)$ denote the vector-valued Sobolev space of square-integrable functions with square-integrable weak derivatives through order two. For $\mathbf{u}\in\mathbf{H}^2(\Omega)$, write $\nabla\mathbf{u}$ for its gradient and $\varepsilon(\mathbf{u})$ for its symmetric gradient.

**Boundary Korn inequality.** There exists a positive constant $\tilde{K}$ such that, for every $\mathbf{u}\in\mathbf{H}^2(\Omega)$,

$$
\|\nabla\mathbf{u}\|^2_{L^2(\Gamma)}\leq\tilde{K}\left[\|\mathbf{u}\|^2_{L^2(\Gamma)}+\|\varepsilon(\mathbf{u})\|^2_{L^2(\Gamma)}\right].
$$

This boundary Korn inequality is used to obtain stability estimates for the elastic Helmholtz equation that are optimal with respect to the frequency $\omega$. It was conjectured in earlier work, and the source provides no resolution, so its status remains open.
source_name: Xiaobing Feng and Cody Lorton, “An unconditionally stable discontinuous Galerkin method for the elastic Helmholtz equations with large frequency”, arXiv:1501.05340 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.05340

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

title: The conjectured strict recurrence inequality for Li coefficients
statement:
Let $\lambda_n$ denote the Li coefficients of the Riemann zeta function. In view of the recurrence relation for these coefficients, **strict recurrence inequality for Li coefficients.** For all integers $n\geq 3$, one has

$$
\lambda_n>2\lambda_{n-1}-\lambda_{n-2}.
$$

The paper presents this as a conjecture following a recurrence relation for Li coefficients. Under the Riemann hypothesis, a related bound is established for the absolute value of $\lambda_n+\lambda_{n-2}-2\lambda_{n-1}$, while the status of this strict inequality itself is not resolved in the supplied text.
source_name: Huan Xiao, “Recurrence relations of Li coefficients”, arXiv:2006.13103 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2006.13103

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2020).

title: Conjectural characterization of tropical characteristic polynomial coefficients for symmetric matrices
statement:
Let $A$ be a symmetric tropical matrix of size $n$, and let $(\delta_0,\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_n)$ be the coefficient sequence of its tropical characteristic polynomial. For $3\leqslant m\leqslant n$, at least one of the following inequalities holds:

$$
\delta_m-\delta_{m-1}\leqslant\delta_{m-1}-\delta_{m-2},
$$

or

$$
\delta_m-\delta_{m-2}\leqslant2(\delta_{m-2}-\delta_{m-3}).
$$

**Conjectural characterization.** For every $m$ with $3\leqslant m\leqslant n$, at least one of these two inequalities holds. The inequalities express a concavity-type regularity in the coefficient sequence of the tropical characteristic polynomial of a symmetric matrix.

The preceding results establish analogous necessary inequalities for the first coefficients, while an example shows that these conditions need not hold for nonsymmetric matrices. Extending the observed pattern to all coefficients is proposed as a direction for future research.
source_name: Dariush Kiani and Hanieh Tavakolipour, “Properties of the Tropical Characteristic Polynomial of Symmetric Matrices”, arXiv:2607.10922 (2026).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.10922

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2026).

title: The integrality and mod 4 reduction conjecture for Muñoz's polynomial
statement:
Let $g$ be a positive integer, let $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$ be the indicated generators of $\mathbb{V}_g$, and write $\beta=\alpha^2+8\varepsilon$ for some $\varepsilon\in\mathbb{V}_g$. Define $n!!=n(n-2)(n-4)\cdots 1$ for positive odd $n$, and let $\zeta_g(\alpha,\beta,\gamma)$ be the polynomial defined recursively by $\zeta_0=1$ and

$$
\zeta_{r+1}=\alpha\zeta_r+r^2(\beta+(-1)^r8)\zeta_{r-1}+4r(r-1)\gamma\zeta_{r-2}.
$$

**The integrality and reduction conjecture.** The expression

$$
\frac{(2g-3)!!}{g!}\zeta_g(\alpha,\alpha^2+8\varepsilon,\gamma)
$$

is a polynomial in $\alpha,\varepsilon,\gamma$ with integer coefficients. Furthermore, its reduction modulo $4$ is congruent to $\pm\alpha^g$.

This proposed statement concerns the integral structure of the invariant part of the instanton Floer ring, whose rational relations are generated by the polynomials $\zeta_g,\zeta_{g+1},\zeta_{g+2}$. The preceding lemma supplies the congruence $\beta\equiv\alpha^2\pmod 8$ needed to formulate it; the source provides no resolution, so its status remains open.
source_name: Christopher Scaduto, “On definite lattices bounded by a homology 3-sphere and Yang-Mills instanton Floer theory”, arXiv:1805.07875 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.07875

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

title: The Minkowski inequality for the discriminant of finite free convolutions
statement:
Let $p$ and $q$ be degree-$d$ polynomials, let $p\boxplus_d q$ denote their finite free convolution, and let $\operatorname{Dis}(p)$ denote the discriminant of $p$. **Minkowski inequality.**

$$
\operatorname{Dis}(p \boxplus_d q)^{\frac{1}{\binom{d}{2}}} \geq \operatorname{Dis}(p)^{\frac{1}{\binom{d}{2}}}+\operatorname{Dis}(q)^{\frac{1}{\binom{d}{2}}}
$$

Equality holds only for generalized Hermite polynomials. This is presented as a broader inequality related to the entropy and log-discriminant of a polynomial; the supplied text does not establish whether the inequality or its equality characterization is proved or remains open.
source_name: Aurelien Gribinski, “A notion of entropy on the roots of polynomials”, arXiv:1907.12826 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.12826

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2019).

title: Extended reverse ultra log-concavity conjecture for adjacent-ratio transposed Boros-Moll sequences
statement: Let $d_\ell(m)$ be the coefficient of $x^\ell$ in the Boros-Moll polynomial $P_m(x)$. For each fixed $\ell\geq 0$, define the sequence $a_m=d_\ell(m-1)d_\ell(m+1)/d_\ell^2(m)$ for $m\geq\ell+1$. A sequence is **extended reverse ultra log-concave** according to the paper's definition of extended ultra log-concavity with all relevant inequalities reversed. **Adjacent-ratio reverse ultra log-concavity conjecture.** For each $\ell\geq 0$, the sequence $\{d_\ell(m-1)d_\ell(m+1)/d_\ell^2(m)\}_{m\geq\ell+1}$ is extended reverse ultra log-concave. This is proposed as a conjecture about the sharp asymptotic behavior of the transposed Boros-Moll sequences, and remains unresolved in the supplied text.
source_name: James J. Y. Zhao, “The extended reverse ultra log-concavity of transposed Boros-Moll sequences”, arXiv:2406.13790 (2024).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.13790

title: Contour-integral bound conjecture on a V-shaped domain
statement:
Let $T$ be the truncation parameter, let $\beta\in[0,2)$ be fixed, and let $z=re^{\pm i\beta\pi/2}$ with $r\in[e^{4+2\beta-2T},1]$. Let $f(u,x)$ and $\delta(u)$ be the functions defined in the paper, and let $\Gamma$ be the positively oriented rectangle

$$
[1-\beta/2,4T^2+1-\beta/2]\times[-ai,ai],\qquad a=2\pi\left(T+\frac12\log r\right).
$$

**Contour-integral bound conjecture.** The remaining contour integral satisfies

$$
\left\lvert\int_\Gamma f(u,x)\delta(u)\,du\right\rvert=\mathcal{O}(e^{-T}).
$$

The claim is presented as being supported by strong numerical evidence and would extend the corresponding contour bound to the V-shaped domain; the supplied text does not provide a proof.
source_name: Astrid Herremans, Daan Huybrechs and Lloyd N. Trefethen, “Resolution of singularities by rational functions”, arXiv:2302.02743 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2302.02743

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2023).

title: Positivity conjecture for fractional Gaussian noise predictor coefficients
statement: Let $H>1/2$, and consider fractional Gaussian noise with Hurst parameter $H$. For any element of this process, project it onto any finite number of its subsequent elements, and denote the resulting projection coefficients by $\Gamma_n^k$, with $2\le k\le n$. **Positivity conjecture.** If $H>1/2$, then all coefficients of these projections are strictly positive. This conjecture concerns the positivity underlying monotonicity properties of the Cholesky decomposition of covariance matrices for fractional Gaussian noise and fractional Brownian motion. Numerical evidence supports it, but the analytic proof remains open, even for certain low-dimensional cases.
source_name: Yuliya Mishura, Kostiantyn Ralchenko and René L. Schilling, “Analytical and computational problems related to fractional Gaussian noise”, arXiv:2209.02501 (2022).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2209.02501

title: Complete monotonicity conjecture for relative entropy in Poisson approximation
statement:
Let $D(P)$ denote the relative entropy of a probability distribution $P$ from the Poisson distribution with the same mean. Write $bi(n,p)$ for the binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$, and $nb(n,p)$ for the negative binomial distribution with parameters $n$ and $p$. A sequence is **completely monotonic** if its finite differences of all orders alternate in sign. Let $\lambda>0$. **Complete monotonicity conjecture.**

$$
D(bi(n, \lambda/n))
$$

should be completely monotonic in $n$ for $n\geq \lambda$, and

$$
D(nb(n, n/(\lambda+n)))
$$

should be completely monotonic in $n$ for $n>0$.

This is a proposed discrete analogue of complete monotonicity results for relative entropy in the central limit theorem. The conjecture is motivated by numerical evidence and extends the paper's monotonicity questions beyond the established results.
source_name: Yaming Yu, “Monotonic Convergence in an Information-Theoretic Law of Small Numbers”, arXiv:0810.5203 (2009).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0810.5203

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2008).

title: Monotonicity conjecture for geometric-scaled sums
statement:
Let ${\boldsymbol X} \equiv \{X_i\}$ be i.i.d. arbitrarily distributed random variables with mean $\lambda$, and let

$$
Y_n \equiv \boxplus_{(\frac{1}{n}, \ldots, \frac{1}{n})}{\boldsymbol X}.
$$

The preceding central limit theorem states that the p.m.f. of $Y_n$ converges to the geometric distribution of mean $\lambda$ as $n\to\infty$. **Entropy monotonicity conjecture.** The entropy $H(Y_n)$ increases monotonically with $n\in\{1,2,\ldots\}$ and converges to the geometric entropy ${\cal E}_g(\lambda)$ as $n\to\infty$. This is analogous to the law of small numbers and to the discrete entropic-monotonicity result for ultra-log-concave random variables, but the conjecture is not restricted to ultra-log-concave random variables; the available result only establishes monotonicity when $n$ increases in power-of-$2$ steps.
source_name: Saikat Guha, Jeffrey H. Shapiro and Raul Garcia-Patron Sanchez, “Thinning, photonic beamsplitting, and a general discrete entropy power inequality”, arXiv:1605.07853 (2016).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.07853

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

title: Monotonic-zero conjecture for incomplete gamma functions
statement: Let $a>0$ be a fixed real number, and let $Q$ denote the first quadrant of the complex plane. A function has **monotonic zeros** in $Q$ when its zeros there, listed by increasing real part, have monotone nondecreasing imaginary parts. **Incomplete-gamma monotonic-zero conjecture.** The incomplete gamma function $\Gamma(z,a)$ has monotonic zeros in $Q$. The source says that computer calculations support this conjecture, while the general zero distribution of $\Gamma(z,a)$ for fixed positive real $a$ is not well understood.
source_name: J. Haglund, “Some conjectures on the zeros of approximates to the Riemann Ξ-function and incomplete gamma functions”, arXiv:0910.5228 (2009).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5228

Status: **open** according to the source (as of October 2009).

title: The normalized frame inequalities for cube sections and cross-polytope projections
statement:
Let $S=\{v_1,\ldots,v_n\}$ be an $(n,k)$-frame spanning $\mathbb{R}^k$, let

$$
B_S=\left(\sum_{i=1}^n v_i\otimes v_i\right)^{-1/2},
$$

and define $P=\operatorname{co}\{\pm v_1,\ldots,\pm v_n\}$ and $Q=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\{x\in\mathbb{R}^k\mid|\langle x,v_i\rangle|\leqslant1\}$. **Normalized frame inequalities.** The conjectured bounds are

$$
C_{\Diamond}(n,k)\mathop{\rm vol}(\Diamond^k)\leqslant\frac{\mathop{\rm vol}P}{\det B_S}\leqslant\mathop{\rm vol}(\Diamond^k);
$$

$$
\mathop{\rm vol}(\Box^k)\leqslant\mathop{\rm vol}(Q)\det B_S\leqslant C_{\Box}(n,k)\mathop{\rm vol}(\Box^k).
$$

These inequalities rewrite the preceding projection and section conjectures in frame language. Since the source does not separately establish their status beyond that of the preceding conjectures, the general assertions remain open.
source_name: G. Ivanov, “On the volume of projections of the cross-polytope”, arXiv:1808.09165 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09165

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2018).

title: Furuta's matrix trace inequality conjecture
statement:
Let $M(n,\mathbb{C})$ be the set of $n\times n$ complex matrices, let $M_h(n,\mathbb{C})$ be the set of Hermitian matrices, and let $M_+(n,\mathbb{C})$ be the set of positive semidefinite matrices. For $X,Y\in M_+(n,\mathbb{C})$, $p\in\mathbb{R}$, and $I$ the identity matrix, consider the two trace inequalities below.

**Furuta's conjecture.** It was asked whether

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\left[(I+X+Y+Y^{1/2}XY^{1/2})^p\right]\leq \operatorname{Tr}\left[(I+X+Y+XY)^p\right]
$$

for $p\geq 1$, and whether

$$
\operatorname{Tr}\left[(I+X+Y+Y^{1/2}XY^{1/2})^p\right]\geq \operatorname{Tr}\left[(I+X+Y+XY)^p\right]
$$

for $0\leq p\leq 1$.

The source paper states that its purpose is to answer this question, so the candidate is presented as a conjectural question rather than an asserted theorem. The surrounding excerpt does not establish whether the question was open at the time of the source paper or whether the source resolves it.
source_name: Shigeru Furuichi and Minghua Lin, “A matrix trace inequality and its application”, arXiv:1001.3803 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1001.3803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2010).

title: Coefficientwise total-positivity conjecture for the four-parameter recurrence triangle
statement:
Let $a,c,d,e$ be algebraic indeterminates, and define $T(n,k)$ by

$$
T(n,k)=[a(n-k)+c]T(n-1,k-1)+(dk+e)T(n-1,k)
$$

for $n\geq 1$, with $T(0,k)=\delta_{k0}$. Thus $\bm{T}=(T(n,k))_{n,k\geq 0}$ is a lower-triangular matrix over $\mathbb{Z}[a,c,d,e]$. A polynomial is nonnegative in the coefficientwise order when all its coefficients are nonnegative, and a polynomial matrix is **coefficientwise totally positive** when all its minors have nonnegative coefficients. **Four-parameter coefficientwise total-positivity conjecture.** The lower-triangular matrix $\bm{T}$ defined by the recurrence above is coefficientwise totally positive in the indeterminates $a,c,d,e$. This conjecture would imply the clean Eulerian and reversed Stirling conjectures under the specializations $(a,c,d,e)=(1,1,1,1)$ and $(1,0,0,1)$, respectively; the source gives no proof of the general assertion.
source_name: Xi Chen, Bishal Deb, Alexander Dyachenko, Tomack Gilmore and Alan D. Sokal, “Coefficientwise total positivity of some matrices defined by linear recurrences”, arXiv:2012.03629 (2020).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.03629

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

title: Relaxation of the parameter condition in the Lieb-type inequalities
statement:
Let $A$ be a positive semi-definite Hermitian matrix, with the block partition and inequalities referred to in the source's Lieb-type theorem and its corollary. The theorem assumes that $\alpha$ is a nonnegative integer or $\alpha\ge n-1$, and establishes several inequalities for $\alpha$- and $-\alpha$-permanents, together with the real-matrix inequality for $\mathrm {per}_{\alpha/2}A$. **Parameter-relaxation conjecture.** The condition on $\alpha$ can be relaxed to

$$
\alpha\ge 1
$$

for all inequalities stated in that theorem and its corollary, except for the leftmost inequality in the displayed two-sided inequality for $(-1)^n\mathrm {per}_{-\alpha}A$. This would extend the stated inequalities beyond the parameter range proved in the theorem, while the supplied text gives no resolution.
source_name: Péter E. Frenkel, “Remarks on the α–permanent”, arXiv:0912.1018 (2009).
references:

title: Strict inner-function inequality conjecture in Hardy spaces
statement:
Let $H^p$ denote the Hardy space on the unit disk, let $d54b$ be the unit circle, and let $f\in H^p$ satisfy $f(0)\neq 0$. An **inner function** is a bounded analytic function on the unit disk whose radial boundary values have modulus one almost everywhere. **Strict inner-function inequality conjecture.** If $J$ is any non-constant inner function, then there exists a constant $c=c_f\in\mathbb{T}$ such that

$$
\|1-Jf\|_p>\|1-cf\|_p.
$$

Such an inequality would strengthen the preceding proposition and would imply that non-trivial optimal polynomial approximants in $H^p$ cannot vanish in the open unit disk. The supplied text gives no resolution of the conjecture.
source_name: Catherine Bénéteau, Raymond Cheng, Christopher Felder, Dmitry Khavinson, Myrto Manolaki and Konstantinos Maronikolakis, “Metric projections, zeros of optimal polynomial approximants, and some extremal problems in Hardy spaces”, arXiv:2511.08000 (2026).
references:

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2025).

title: Dimension-free trace commutator inequality
statement:
Let $A$ and $B$ be positive definite matrices satisfying $\operatorname{Tr}(A+B)=1$. **Trace commutator conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$, independent of the dimensions of $A$ and $B$, such that

$$
\lVert[B,\log(A+B)]\rVert_1\leq c\bigl(-\operatorname{Tr}A\log\operatorname{Tr}A-\operatorname{Tr}B\log\operatorname{Tr}B\bigr).
$$

The source says that numerical work suggests the sharper value $c=1$, and gives a reduction to the corresponding inequality for arbitrary positive semidefinite matrices; neither the existence claim nor the sharp constant is resolved there.
source_name: K. M. R. Audenaert and F. Kittaneh, “Problems and Conjectures in Matrix and Operator Inequalities”, arXiv:1201.5232 (2012).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.5232

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2012).

title: Costa–Cover conjecture on the concavity of parallel volume
statement:
Let $A$ be a bounded measurable set in $cmathbb{R}^n$, let $B_2^n$ denote the Euclidean closed unit ball, and let $|\cdot|$ denote Lebesgue measure. **Costa–Cover conjecture.** The function

$$
t \mapsto |A+tB_2^n|^{\frac{1}{n}}
$$

is concave on $\mathbb{R}_+$. This conjecture is the parallel-volume analogue of the concavity of entropy power and concerns a Brunn–Minkowski-type property for Euclidean outer parallel sets; its resolution status is not specified in the source.
source_name: Arnaud Marsiglietti, “Concavity properties of extensions of the parallel volume”, arXiv:1306.6899 (2014).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1302.6093](https://arxiv.org/abs/1302.6093).

title: Measure classification from monotonicity of boundary content under Minkowski addition
statement:
Let $n\geq 2$, let $\mu$ be a Radon measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and write $\mu^+(\partial K)$ for the boundary-content functional used in the source. Assume that for every convex body $K$ and every compact, convex set $L$ containing the origin,

$$
\mu^+(\partial(K+L))\geq\mu^+(\partial K).
$$

**Measure-classification conjecture.** Then $\mu$ is a constant multiple of Lebesgue measure.

This proposed extension of the one-dimensional result would recover the classification of Lebesgue measure in higher dimensions. The supplied text presents it as an unresolved question and gives no resolution.
source_name: Matthieu Fradelizi, Dylan Langharst, Mokshay Madiman and Artem Zvavitch, “Weighted Brunn-Minkowski Theory II: Inequalities for Mixed Measures and Applications”, arXiv:2402.10314 (2026).

title: Log-concavity of the coefficients of the complete-quadrics polynomial
statement: For a fixed positive integer $a$, let $\phi(a,n)$ denote the polynomial in $n$ given by the degree of the inverse of a general $a$-dimensional linear space of symmetric $n\times n$ matrices. Do the coefficients of $\phi(a,n)$, viewed as a polynomial in $n$, form a log-concave sequence?

title: Monotonicity of a conformal heat-trace functional
statement: Let $(S^n,g)$ be the round sphere, let $Y=\Delta_{S^n}+\frac n2\left(\frac n2-1\right)$ be the Yamabe operator, and let $W$ be a positive smooth function on $S^n$ normalized by $\int_{S^n}W^{n/2}=\operatorname{vol}(S^n,g)$. Define $Y_W=W^{-1/2}YW^{-1/2}$ on $L^2(S^n,g)$ and $f_W(t)=t^{n/2}\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-tY_W})$. **Conjecture:** If $n\ge 4$, then $f_W(t)$ is decreasing in $t$ for $t>0$.

title: Robin gap monotonicity
statement: For a convex bounded domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$, is the Robin spectral gap, given by the difference between the first two Robin eigenvalues, namely $(\rho_2-\rho_1)(\alpha)$, strictly increasing as a function of the Robin parameter $\alpha>0$?
source_name: Oberwolfach Reports: 10.4171/OWR/2023/36, page 82

title: Monotonicity of the spectral gap
statement:
For a bounded convex domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$, the spectral gap $\lambda_2(\Omega, \alpha)-\lambda_1(\Omega, \alpha)$ is strictly increasing as a function of $\alpha>0$. In particular, the Neumann gap provides a lower bound for the Dirichlet gap:

$$
\mu_1(\Omega)<\lambda_2(\Omega)-\lambda_1(\Omega).
$$
source_name: AimPL: Shape optimization with surface interactions (posed by R. Smits)

title: The function-approximation conjecture for operator monotone functions
statement:
Let $\widehat{\mathcal M}_+$ be the space of Fourier transforms of finite positive Borel measures on $\mathbb R$, and define

$$
E_f(c)=\inf_{g'\in\widehat{\mathcal M}_+}\left(\sup_{x\geq0}(f-g)(x)-\inf_{x\geq0}(f-g)(x)+cg'(0)\right).
$$

Let $f$ be a non-negative function that is operator monotone on $[0,\infty)$. **The function-approximation conjecture.** For every $c>0$,

$$
E_f(c)\leq Cf(c)
$$

with $C=1$. This conjecture is introduced as implying the normalized commutator inequality in the case $A=B$; its resolution is not stated in the supplied excerpt.
source_name: David Herrera, “On the commutator modulus of continuity for operator monotone functions”, arXiv:2311.17448 (2023).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.17448

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2023).

title: Conjecture for Stirling cycle numbers of all orders
statement:
Let $C^{(r)}$ be the Stirling cycle triangle of order $r$, let

$$
\widecheck{C}^{(r)}=\left(C^{(r)}\right)^{\rm rev}
$$

be the triangle formed by reversing the rows of $C^{(r)}$, and let $c_{r,n}(x)$ be its row-generating polynomials. A sequence of polynomials is **coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive** in $x$ when every minor of its Hankel matrix has coefficients that are nonnegative in $x$. **Conjecture for Stirling cycle numbers of all orders.** The following are true: (a) $C^{(r)}$ is totally positive for all $r\geq 1$. (b) $\widecheck{C}^{(r)}$ is totally positive for $r=1,2$ and is not totally positive when $r\geq 3$. (c) The polynomials $c_{r,n}(x)$ are negative-real-rooted for $r=1,2$ and have non-real complex zeros for $r\geq 3$ and $n\geq 3$. Also, the row sequences of $C^{(r)}$ are log-concave for $1\leq r\leq 5$. (d) The sequence $(c_{r,n}(x))_{n\geq 0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive in $x$ for all $r\geq 1$. These assertions refine the known low-order relationship between Stirling cycle triangles and Eulerian-type triangles; the cases $r\geq 3$ include both failures of row-reversed total positivity and non-real-rootedness, while the total positivity of $C^{(r)}$ and the Hankel property are asserted for every order.
source_name: Bishal Deb and Alan D. Sokal, “Higher-order Stirling cycle and subset triangles: Total positivity, continued fractions and real-rootedness”, arXiv:2507.18959 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.18959

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2025).

title: Conjecture on ultra-log-concave intrinsic-volume sequences
statement:
Let $(a_k)_{k\geq 0}$ be a sequence of positive numbers with $a_0=1$. An infinite-dimensional GB-set is a set for which the intrinsic volumes $\{V_k(K)\}_{k\geq 0}$ form such a sequence.

**Conjecture on ultra-log-concave intrinsic-volume sequences.** The sequence $(a_k)_{k\geq 0}$ is the intrinsic-volume sequence of some infinite-dimensional GB-set if and only if

$$
a_k^2\geq\frac{k+1}{k}a_{k-1}a_{k+1},\qquad k=1,2,\dots.
$$

Thus, ultra-log-concavity is conjectured to be not only necessary but also sufficient for an infinite-dimensional intrinsic-volume sequence. The source presents this as an open analogue of the Blaschke problem in Hilbert space; no resolution is supplied.
source_name: Maria Dospolova, Mikhail Germanskov and Dmitry Zaporozhets, “On Steiner entire function”, arXiv:2507.11626 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.11626

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of July 2025). “Therefore, any GB-set with $\rho(K) > \frac{2}{3}$ provides a counterexample to the Gao--Vitale conjecture.”

title: The threshold conjecture for concavity of stable distributions
statement:
A strictly stable probability measure is a stable law, and a probability measure is **convex** when it satisfies the paper's convexity property for measures. In finite dimensions, fix $\kappa\leq 0$ and let $\alpha^*(\kappa,n)\in(0,2]$ depend only on $\kappa$ and $n$. **Threshold conjecture for concavity of stable distributions.** Any strictly stable probability measure on an infinite-dimensional separable Hilbert space is convex. In the finite-dimensional case, a spherically symmetric stable distribution of index $\alpha$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ is $\kappa$-concave if and only if

$$
\alpha\geq\alpha^*(\kappa,n).
$$

The conjecture predicts both an infinite-dimensional convexity phenomenon and a sharp threshold in finite dimensions. The surrounding discussion gives partial negative information for symmetric stable laws but does not establish the claimed threshold.
source_name: Sergey Bobkov and Mokshay Madiman, “The entropy per coordinate of a random vector is highly constrained under convexity conditions”, arXiv:1006.2883 (2010).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1006.2883

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2010).
